newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia seen maintaining rice self-sufficiency.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seen maintaining rice self-sufficiency.

text.p: Indonesia will be able to maintain self-sufficiency in rice despite predictions it will become a rice importer beyond the year 2000, a senior official in Indonesia's Agriculture Ministry said on Thursday.

Faisal Kasryno, director-general of the Agency for Agricultural Research and Development in the ministry, said at the Asia rice conference in Singapore economic progress and efficient farming methods should help Jakarta stave off imports.
The use of technology to enable farmers to use one million hectares of acidic land in central Kalimantan and declining consumption by increasingly prosperous Indonesians should help.
"Efforts to optimise use of natural resources and the use of capital intensive and advanced technologies in rice farming...will keep Indonesia self-sufficient in rice," he said.
The Indonesian official added that an additional 39 million hectares in Sumatra, Irian Jaya and Kalimantan could be harnessed for rice production.
"Developing these soils for crop production can reduce pressure on habitat-rich forests and on fragile and marginal land areas," he said.

The U.S. Agriculture Department and other analysts in Indonesia have predicted that the country will become a net rice importer by 2000. Imports are predicted to reach 842,000 tonnes annually by 2000 and rise to about 982,000 tonnes in 2010.
Rice is the staple food of 97 percent of Indonesia's 200 million people.
